steps.label: The hidden layer turns XOR into separable features · 1
steps.speakerNotes: The positive inputs zero-one and one-zero both map to hidden coordinates one-one; the ring denotes two overlapping samples. Zero-zero maps to zero-one and one-one maps to one-zero. An AND gate separates the positive hidden position, using the stated convention at zero.

steps.label: Remove the steps and these weights cancel · 1
steps.speakerNotes: These particular weights cancel, giving minus 1.5 under identity activations. General all-linear networks need not be constant. The source’s claim of less than half of XOR is not retained: thresholding this constant at zero would classify two of the four points correctly.

steps.label: More all-linear layers still form one linear map · 1
steps.speakerNotes: This page concerns bias-free linear maps. Their product is one matrix, so depth does not enlarge the represented function class. Parameterization and optimization can still differ; training behavior is not asserted identical.

steps.label: The same weights give different contours after changing activation · 1
steps.speakerNotes: The source seed-two 2-4-3-1 network has fixed weights and no biases. Only the two hidden activations change; output stays linear. We draw the source numerical contour at 1e-9. Large exactly-zero ReLU regions mean it is not an ordinary exact zero boundary. No four-region guarantee, training or generalization claim is made.
